thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: GeoDNS mismatch detected for api.redwood-inference.com. Elevated HTTP 502/504 from EU region. Suspect: Cloudflare edge returning deprecated EU pool IPs. Detected 03:12 UTC.

marco: paging @oncall-raj and @sre-anya. EU customers reporting failures.

oncall-raj: ack, joining. pulling logs and dns traces.

sre-anya: quick check: origin health is fine, LB metrics normal. But multiple public resolvers returning an IP set that was removed last week (old eu-west-2 pool). TTLs on answers vary widely, some show 7200s.

olga: got a customer dig from Vodafone resolver:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.10.6 <<>> +short api.redwood-inference.com @80.58.61.250
13.52.34.11
```
olga: that ip is from our decommissioned eu pool.

netops-kyle: CF dashboard shows edge nodes in EU reattaching stale assignments after config deployment. Opening CF ticket; also seeing anomalous EDNS subnet behavior.

incident-bot: Cloudflare ticket created: CF-78910.

oncall-raj: mitigation options: 1) force purge CF geo caches, 2) temporarily modify authoritative answers to include only active EU VIPs (via Route53 override), 3) lower TTL to short window. Thoughts?

marco: prefer least-risk path: purge + lower TTL. If that doesn't converge in 5-10m then Route53 override.

sre-anya: lowering TTL now to 30s for geo records in console -> applied. Pushing CF cache purge for domain and zone-level geo cache.

support-maya: notifying impacted customers with ETA ~10m for mitigation.

netops-kyle: CF acknowledged the ticket; they claim an internal mapping rebuild is in progress and purges should help. They flagged affected POPs.

olga: monitoring: EU error-rate trending down from 18% -> 7% in 4m. Still some resolvers returning old IPs.

oncall-raj: performing distributed dig checks from several public resolvers:
- 1.1.1.1 -> 52.18.9.10 (good)
- 80.58.61.250 -> 13.52.34.11 (stale)
- 8.8.8.8 -> 52.18.9.11 (good)
marco: indicates resolver cache heterogeneity. We'll likely see intermittent client impacts until caches expire or are purged.

sre-anya: preparing Route53-only failover plan in case CF purges + TTL change don't resolve within 12m: create temporary geo record set that answers EU resolvers directly from Route53 authoritative name servers with only active EU A records; keep change window small and document rollback.

incident-bot: plan noted. Severity set to P2. Incident start=1766543210.

netops-kyle: CF engineer says rebuild finished for some POPs; they're running zone-wide recompute now. Asking for any resolver IPs still returning stale answers.

olga: shared list of 6 resolver IPs in support ticket.

support-maya: support update sent at 03:24 UTC: "We are seeing partial reachability in EU due to DNS caching at some ISPs. Mitigation underway; ETA 10-20 minutes."

marco: after 9 minutes error rate down to 2.1%, customer sessions recovering.

oncall-raj: Im inclined to hold off on Route53 override for now. CF purge + TTL reduction + their rebuild seems to be working. Keeping monitoring + short TTL for 45 more minutes.

sre-anya: creating a temporary synthetic monitor that checks Geo answers across 12 public resolvers every 30s to detect skew. Alert threshold: >5% mismatch -> automatic escalation.

netops-kyle: CF ticket updated requesting RCA and confirmation they won't reintroduce old assignments. Also asked them to confirm if internal rollback triggered this.

support-maya: customers informed of improved status at 03:35 UTC. No immediate escalations.

marco: handing off to @netops-kyle for overnight follow-up; I'll draft post-incident notes.

netops-kyle: taking handoff. Actions: 1) keep TTL=30 for 45m, 2) maintain synthetic monitor, 3) follow CF ticket to closure and request RCA + timeline for fixed mapping, 4) consider Route53 override playbook if recurrence within 24h.

incident-bot: Incident marked resolved (mitigation in place) at 03:40 UTC. Close when postmortem created. Link: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/geo-dns-1766543210

marco: will open postmortem and assign to @sre-anya and @netops-kyle. Thanks for fast response team :thumbsup:

support-maya: final note: all affected customers notified.

sre-anya: recommend follow-up item: add GeoDNS answer-consistency checks to weekly chaos tests.

oncall-raj: good catch, good work everyone.
